Appendix A Some series expansions involving Stirling numbers, Gregory’s coefficients, Cauchy numbers, Bernoulli numbers, binomial coefficients and harmonic numbers

In this first supplementary part of our work, we give the proofs of some of the results given in Section II.2. First of all, we show that Fontana–Mascheroni’s formula (12) may be readily derived from the generating equations for the Stirling numbers. The proof is similar to (41):

∑n=1∞(−1)n−1n⋅1n!∑l=1nS1​(n,l)l+1=−∑n=1∞1n!⋅∑l=1n(−1)l​|S1​(n,l)|l+1∫01xn−1dx=∑l=1∞(−1)l+1l+1∫01[∑n=1∞|S1​(n,l)|n!​xn]⏟see (15)d​xx=−∑l=1∞1(l+1)!∫01lnl⁡(1−x)x​dx⏟see (41)=∑l=1∞(−1)l+1⋅ζ⁡(l+1)l+1=γ\begin{array}[]{c}\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\!\frac{\,(-1)^{n-1}\,}{n}\cdot\frac{1}{\,n!\,}\!\sum_{l=1}^{n}\!\frac{\,S_{1}(n,l)\,}{l+1}\,=\,-\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\!\frac{1}{\,n!\,}\cdot\!\sum_{l=1}^{n}\!\frac{\,(-1)^{l}\big|S_{1}(n,l)\big|\,}{l+1}\!\int\limits_{0}^{1}\!x^{n-1}dx\\[22.76219pt] \displaystyle\,=\,\sum_{l=1}^{\infty}\!\frac{(-1)^{l+1}}{\,l+1\,}\!\int\limits_{0}^{1}\!\underbrace{\left[\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\!\frac{\,\big|S_{1}(n,l)\big|\,}{n!}x^{n}\right]}_{\text{see \eqref{h37qp2b237ds}}}\!\frac{dx}{x}\,=\,-\sum_{l=1}^{\infty}\!\frac{1}{\,(l+1)!\,}\!\underbrace{\int\limits_{0}^{1}\!\frac{\ln^{l}(1-x)}{x}\,dx}_{\text{see \eqref{kljd023jdnr2}}}\\[22.76219pt] \displaystyle\,=\,\sum_{l=1}^{\infty}\!\frac{(-1)^{l+1}\!\cdot\zeta(l+1)}{\,l+1\,}\,=\,\gamma\end{array} (96)

in virtue of known Euler’s representation for γ\gamma, see e.g. [8, vol. I, p. 45, Eq. 1.17(3)] or put simply z=1z=1 into Legendre’s series (8). The above derivation may be readily generalized to

∑n=1∞(−1)n−1n⋅n!​∑l=1nf⁡(l)​S1​(n,l)=∑l=1∞(−1)l+1​f​(l)​ζ​(l+1),\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\!\frac{\,(-1)^{n-1}\,}{\,n\cdot n!\,}\!\sum_{l=1}^{n}f(l)\,S_{1}(n,l)\,=\,\sum_{l=1}^{\infty}(-1)^{l+1}f(l)\zeta(l+1)\,,

where f⁡(l)f(l) is an arbitrary function providing the convergence. In particular, taking f⁡(l)=1/(l+k)f(l)=1/(l+k), the above equation reduces to

∑n=1∞(−1)n−1n⋅n!∑l=1nS1​(n,l)l+k=∑l=2∞(−1)l⋅ζ⁡(l)l+k−1,k=1,2,3,…\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\!\frac{\,(-1)^{n-1}\,}{\,n\cdot n!\,}\!\sum_{l=1}^{n}\!\frac{\,S_{1}(n,l)\,}{l+k}\,=\,\sum_{l=2}^{\infty}\!\frac{(-1)^{l}\!\cdot\zeta(l)}{\,l+k-1\,}\,,\qquad\qquad k=1,2,3,\ldots (97)

the series on the left converging as ∑n−2​ln−k−1​n\,\sum n^{-2}\ln^{-k-1}\!n\,, see (B.2). As concerns the series in the right–hand side, it can be always expressed in terms of elementary functions, Euler’s constant γ\gamma, the ζ\zeta–function and its first–order derivatives. For instance, integrating Legendre’s series (8) over z∈[0,1]z\in[0,1] and using Raabe’s formula, see e.g. [8, vol. I, p. 24, Eq. 1.9.1(18)], [14, p. 552, Eq. (30)], we get

∑l=2∞(−1)l⋅ζ⁡(l)l⁡(l+1)=γ+ln⁡2​π2−1\sum_{l=2}^{\infty}\!\frac{(-1)^{l}\!\cdot\zeta(l)}{\,l(l+1)\,}\,=\,\frac{\,\gamma+\ln 2\pi\,}{2}-1 (98)

By partial fraction decomposition and using again above Euler’s representation for γ\gamma, we find

∑l=2∞(−1)l⋅ζ⁡(l)l+1=γ−ln⁡2​π2+1\sum_{l=2}^{\infty}\!\frac{(-1)^{l}\!\cdot\zeta(l)}{\,l+1\,}\,=\,\frac{\,\gamma-\ln 2\pi\,}{2}+1 (99)

so that for k=2k=2

∑n=1∞(−1)n−1n⋅n!​∑l=1nS1​(n,l)l+2=γ−ln⁡2​π2+1\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\!\frac{\,(-1)^{n-1}\,}{\,n\cdot n!\,}\!\sum_{l=1}^{n}\!\frac{\,S_{1}(n,l)\,}{l+2}\,=\,\frac{\,\gamma-\ln 2\pi\,}{2}+1 (100)

which converges as ∑n−2​ln−3​n\,\sum n^{-2}\ln^{-3}\!n\,, see (139). Proceeding analogously and replacing Raabe’s formula by the (k−2)(k-2)th–order moment of ln⁡Γ⁡(z)\ln\Gamma(z), see [44, p. 175, (6.14)],4141 41 Expression for the first–order moment may be also found in [14, p. 552]. we obtain for k=2,3,4,…k=2,3,4,\ldots

Finally, as we noticed in Section II, Stirling numbers of the first kind may also appear in the evaluation of certain integrals, which, at first sight, have nothing to do with Stirling numbers. For instance, it is known that some particular cases of ∫lns⁡(1−x)​x−k​𝑑x\int\ln^{s}(1-x)\,x^{-k}\,dx\, taken between x=0x=0 and x=1x=1 reduce to ζ\zeta--function and to elementary functions.4545 45 Various particular cases of this integral appear in numerous texbooks, see e.g. [149, no 2147], By using Stirling numbers, we can show that more generally, if kk is integer and the integral is convergent, then the latter may be always reduced to a finite set of ζ\zeta–functions with coefficients containing Stirling numbers of the first kind and binomial coefficients. This can be shown as follows. By differentiating kk times the well–known expansion (1−y)−1=∑yn\,(1-y)^{-1}=\sum y^{n}, we get

1(1−y)k+1=1k!∑n=k∞n(n−1)⋯(n−k+1)yn−k=1k!∑n=k∞∑r=1kS1(k,r)nryn−k,|y|<1,\frac{1}{(1-y)^{k+1}}\,=\,\frac{1}{k!}\sum_{n=k}^{\infty}n(n-1)\cdots(n-k+1)\,y^{n-k}=\,\frac{1}{k!}\sum_{n=k}^{\infty}\sum_{r=1}^{k}S_{1}(k,r)\,n^{r}y^{n-k}\,,\qquad|y|<1\,,

in virtue of (14b). Rewriting this result for y=e−ty=e^{-t}, multiplying it by e−te^{-t} and putting k−1k-1 instead of kk, yields

e−t(1−e−t)k=1(k−1)!​∑n=k−1∞∑r=1k−1S1​(k−1,r)​nr​e−(n−k+2)​t,0<t<∞\frac{e^{-t}}{\big(1-e^{-t}\big)^{k}}\,=\,\frac{1}{(k-1)!}\!\!\sum_{n=k-1}^{\infty}\!\sum_{r=1}^{k-1}S_{1}(k-1,r)\,n^{r}e^{-(n-k+2)t}\,,\qquad 0<t<\infty

Consider now the integral in question. Making a change of variable x=1−e−t\,x=1-e^{-t}, employing the above expansion and performing the term–by–term integration, we have

∫01lns⁡(1−x)xk​𝑑x=(−1)s​∫0∞ts​e−t​d​t(1−e−t)k=(−1)s(k−1)!​∑n=k−1∞∑r=1k−1S1​(k−1,r)​nr​∫0∞ts​e−(n−k+2)​t​dt⏟Γ⁡(s+1)⋅(n−k+2)−s−1=(−1)s⋅Γ⁡(s+1)(k−1)!​∑r=1k−1S1​(k−1,r)​∑n=k−1∞nr(n−k+2)s+1\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\int\limits_{0}^{1}\!\frac{\,\ln^{s}(1-x)\,}{x^{k}}\,dx&\displaystyle\,=(-1)^{s}\!\!\int\limits_{0}^{\infty}\frac{\,t^{s}e^{-t}dt\,}{\big(1-e^{-t}\big)^{k}}\,=\,\frac{(-1)^{s}}{(k-1)!}\!\!\sum_{n=k-1}^{\infty}\!\sum_{r=1}^{k-1}S_{1}(k-1,r)\,n^{r}\!\!\!\underbrace{\int\limits_{0}^{\infty}\!t^{s}e^{-(n-k+2)t}dt}_{\Gamma(s+1)\cdot(n-k+2)^{-s-1}}\\[17.07164pt] &\displaystyle=\,\frac{\,(-1)^{s}\!\cdot\Gamma(s+1)\,}{(k-1)!}\sum_{r=1}^{k-1}S_{1}(k-1,r)\!\!\!\sum_{n=k-1}^{\infty}\!\!\frac{n^{r}}{(n-k+2)^{s+1}}\end{array}

Changing the summation index n=p+k−2n=p+k-2 and using the binomial expansion, the latter series becomes

∑n=k−1∞nr(n−k+2)l+s=∑p=1∞(p+k−2)rps+1=∑m=0r(rm)​(k−2)r−m​ζ​(s+1−m)\sum_{n=k-1}^{\infty}\!\!\frac{n^{r}}{(n-k+2)^{l+s}}\,=\,\sum_{p=1}^{\infty}\frac{(p+k-2)^{r}}{p^{s+1}}\,=\,\sum_{m=0}^{r}\!\binom{r}{m}(k-2)^{r-m}\zeta(s+1-m)

Appendix B Bounds and full asymptotical expansions for some special numbers which appeared in Section II

B.1 Bounds and full asymptotical expansion for the Cauchy numbers of the second kind C2,nC_{2,n}, also known as generalized Bernoulli numbers |Bn(n)|\big|B_{n}^{(n)}\big|\,

Consider the Cauchy numbers of the second kind, which appear in series expansions for ln⁡ln⁡2\ln\ln 2, z(1+z)​ln⁡(1+z)\frac{z}{(1+z)\ln(1+z)} and ln⁡ln⁡(1+z)\ln\ln(1+z), equations (11), (19) and (20) respectively. Using definition (14), we may reduce it to a definite integral

(6)–(7), Fig. 2]. Remarking that on the unit interval the function 1/Γ⁡(x)1/\Gamma(x) is nonnegative and may be bounded from below and from above as

These bounds are sharper than (121), but weaker than (120); Fig. 7 illustrates their quality. It therefore also follows that series (11) for ln⁡ln⁡2\,\ln\ln 2\, converges at the same rate as ∑(−1)n​(n​ln⁡n)−1\,\sum(-1)^{n}(n\ln n)^{-1}\,.

+{− 6​(1−γ)(n−1)​ln4⁡(n−1)+ 1−γn⁡(n−1)​ln2⁡(n−1)+ 2​(3−γ)n⁡(n−1)​ln3⁡(n−1)+ 12​(1−γ)n⁡(n−1)​ln4⁡(n−1)}\displaystyle\qquad\displaystyle+\left\{-\frac{\,6\,(1-\gamma)\,}{\,(n-1)\ln^{4}(n-1)\,}\,+\,\frac{\,1-\gamma\,\,}{\,n(n-1)\ln^{2}(n-1)\,}+\,\frac{\,2\,(3-\gamma)\,\,}{\,n(n-1)\ln^{3}(n-1)\,}+\,\frac{\,12\,(1-\gamma)\,\,}{\,n(n-1)\ln^{4}(n-1)\,}\right\}

Since the contribution of the terms in curly brackets is negative for n>4.921304199​…n>4.921304199\ldots  (thanks to the leading first term), the above bounds also imply a weaker relation

 1n​ln2​n− 2n​ln3​n⩽|Gn|⩽ 1(n−1)​ln2⁡(n−1)− 2​γ(n−1)​ln3⁡(n−1),n⩾5.\frac{\,1\,}{\,n\ln^{2}\!n\,}\,-\,\frac{\,2\,}{\,n\ln^{3}\!n\,}\leqslant\,\big|G_{n}\big|\,\leqslant\,\frac{\,1\,}{\,(n-1)\ln^{2}(n-1)\,}\,-\,\frac{\,2\gamma\,}{\,(n-1)\ln^{3}(n-1)\,}\,,\qquad\quad n\geqslant 5\,. (129)

Moreover, the detailed study of the right part in (128) leads to another inequalities

 1n​ln2​n− 2n​ln3​n⩽|Gn|⩽ 1n​ln2​n− 2​γn​ln3​n,n⩾5,\frac{\,1\,}{\,n\ln^{2}\!n\,}\,-\,\frac{\,2\,}{\,n\ln^{3}\!n\,}\leqslant\,\big|G_{n}\big|\,\leqslant\,\frac{\,1\,}{\,n\ln^{2}\!n\,}\,-\,\frac{\,2\gamma\,}{\,n\ln^{3}\!n\,}\,,\qquad\quad n\geqslant 5\,, (130)

which are slightly stronger and simpler than (129), but weaker than parent inequalities (128). Graphical simulations, see Fig. 8, show that bounds (130) are very sharp and their accuracy should be sufficient for most of the situations..

Making n→∞n\to\infty yields the first–order approximation for Gregory’s coefficients: |Gn|∼1n​ln2​n|G_{n}|\sim\frac{1}{n\ln^{2}n}\,. Higher–order terms of this asymptotics may be found as follows. By (13), the last integral in (127) becomes

(−1)n−1​∫01(1−z)​Γ​(n−1+z)Γ⁡(z)​dz==(−1)n−1(n−1)!∫01(1−z)​nz−1Γ⁡(z){1+(1−z)​(2−z)2​n+O(n−2)}dz,n→∞,\begin{array}[]{ll}&\displaystyle(-1)^{n-1}\!\int\limits_{0}^{1}\!\frac{\,(1-z)\,\Gamma(n-1+z)\,}{\Gamma(z)}\,dz=\\[17.07164pt] &\displaystyle\qquad\quad=\,(-1)^{n-1}(n-1)!\!\int\limits_{0}^{1}\!\frac{\,(1-z)\,n^{z-1}\,}{\Gamma(z)}\left\{1+\frac{\,(1-z)\,(2-z)\,}{2n}+O(n^{-2})\right\}dz\,,\qquad n\to\infty\,,\end{array}

Then, using the MacLaurin series for 1/Γ⁡(z)1/\Gamma(z) and proceeding analogously to (125), we find

Gn=1n!​∑l=1nS1​(n,l)l+1\displaystyle\displaystyle G_{n}\,=\,\frac{1}{n!}\sum_{l=1}^{n}\frac{S_{1}(n,l)}{l+1}\; =(−1)n−1n⋅∑l=1∞(−1)llnl+1⁡n⋅[1−xΓ⁡(x)]x=1(l)+O⁡(1n2​ln⁡n)\displaystyle\displaystyle=\,\frac{\,(-1)^{n-1}}{n}\cdot\sum\limits_{l=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{l}}{\ln^{l+1}n}\cdot\left[\frac{1-x}{\Gamma(x)}\right]^{(l)}_{x=1}+O\!\left(\frac{1}{\,n^{2}\ln n\,}\right) (131)
=(−1)n−1n⋅{1ln2⁡n−2​γln3⁡n−π2−6​γ2 2​ln4​n+O⁡(1ln5⁡n)}\displaystyle\displaystyle=\,\frac{\,(-1)^{n-1}}{n}\cdot\left\{\frac{1}{\,\ln^{2}\!n\,}-\frac{2\gamma}{\,\ln^{3}\!n\,}-\frac{\,\pi^{2}-6\gamma^{2}}{\,2\ln^{4}\!n\,}+O\!\left(\frac{1}{\,\ln^{5}\!n\,}\right)\!\right\}

Historical remark The first–order approximation for Gregory’s coefficients GnG_{n} at n→∞n\to\infty, the first formulæ in (21), was found by Ernst Schröder in 1879 [134, p. 115, Eq. (25a)]. It was rediscovered by Johan Steffensen in 1924 [144, pp. 2–4], [145, pp. 106–107], and was slightly bettered in 1957 by Davis [41, p. 14, Eq. (14)]. Higher–order terms of this asymptotics were obtained by S. C. Van Veen in 1950 [151, p. 336], [113, p. 29], Gergő Nemes in 2011 [106] and the author in 2014. S. C. Van Veen and Gergő Nemes used different methods to derive their results and obtained different expressions; however, one can show that their formulæ are equivalent. The former employed an elegant contour integration method, while the latter used Watson’s lemma. Our formula (131) differs from both Van Veen’s result and Nemes’ result, but it is also equivalent to them. Note also that many researchers (e.g. Nørlund [113, p. 29], Davis [41, p. 14, Eq. (14)], Nemes [106]) incorrectly attribute this asymptotics to Steffensen, who only rediscovered it. The same asymptotics also appears in the well–known monograph [38, p. 294], but Comtet did not specify the source of the formula. As regards the bounds for GnG_{n}, in 1922 Steffensen found that

 1 6​n​(n−1)<|Gn|< 1 6​n,n>2,\frac{\,1\,}{\,6n\,(n-1)\,}<\,\big|G_{n}\big|\,<\,\frac{\,1\,}{\,6n\,}\,,\qquad\quad n>2\,,

[143, p. 198, Eq. (27)], [144, p. 2, Eq. (3)], [145, p. 106, Eq. (9)]. A stronger result (at large nn) was stated by Kluyver in 1924

|Gn|<1n​ln⁡n,n⩾2,\big|G_{n}\big|\,<\,\frac{1}{\,n\ln n\,}\,,\qquad\quad n\geqslant 2\,,

[78, p. 144]. In 2010, Rubinstein [123, p. 30, Theorem 1.1] found a bound for more general numbers, from which it inter alia follows that4949 49 Rubinstein’s αn​(s)\alpha_{n}(s) at s=0s=0 are our −|Gn|-\big|G_{n}\big|.

|Gn|⩽ 4​(1+ln⁡(1+n))1+n,n⩾1.\big|G_{n}\big|\,\leqslant\frac{\,4\,(1+\ln(1+n))\,}{1+n}\,,\qquad\quad n\geqslant 1\,.

This bound is nevertheless much weaker than both preceeding bounds. In another recent paper [37, p. 473], Coffey remarked that numerical simulations suggest that |Gn|\big|G_{n}\big| should be lesser than 1n​ln2​n\,\frac{1}{n\ln^{2}n}\, for all n⩾2n\geqslant 2, but that the proof of this result was missing.5050 50 Note that Coffey’s pn+1p_{n+1} are our |Gn||G_{n}| (Coffey’s notation are probably borrowed from Ser’s paper [135]). Inequalities (130) include the missing proof. By the way, as far as we know, our bounds (128)–(130) are currently the best bounds for Gregory’s coefficients.

Nota Bene Analogously, one can show that more general results take place. For instance, for positive integer kk

∑l=1n|S1​(n,l)|l+k=∫01xk−1​(x)n​𝑑x∼(n−1)!​∫01nx​xk−1Γ⁡(x)​𝑑x,n→∞.\sum_{l=1}^{n}\frac{\,\big|S_{1}(n,l)\big|\,}{l+k}\,=\int\limits_{0}^{1}\!x^{k-1}(x)_{n}\,dx\,\sim\,(n-1)!\!\int\limits_{0}^{1}\!\frac{\,n^{x}x^{k-1}\,}{\Gamma(x)}\,dx\,,\qquad n\to\infty\,.

Whence, using (69)–(70) and (124), we obtain

1n!​∑l=1n|S1​(n,l)|l+k\displaystyle\displaystyle\frac{1}{n!}\sum_{l=1}^{n}\frac{\big|S_{1}(n,l)\big|}{l+k}\;\, ∼1ln⁡n+∑l=1∞(−1)llnl+1⁡n⋅[xk−1Γ⁡(x)]x=1(l)=1ln⁡n−k−1+γln2⁡n\displaystyle\displaystyle\sim\,\frac{1}{\,\ln n\,}+\sum\limits_{l=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{l}}{\ln^{l+1}n}\cdot\left[\frac{x^{k-1}}{\Gamma(x)}\right]^{(l)}_{x=1}=\,\frac{1}{\,\ln n\,}-\frac{\,k-1+\gamma\,}{\,\ln^{2}\!n\,}
+ 6​γ2+12​γ​(k−1)−π2+6​(k2−3​k+2) 6​ln3​n+O⁡(1ln4⁡n),k=1,2,3,…n→∞.\displaystyle\displaystyle\quad+\,\frac{\,6\gamma^{2}+12\gamma(k-1)-\pi^{2}+6(k^{2}-3k+2)\,}{\,6\ln^{3}\!n\,}+O\!\left(\frac{1}{\,\ln^{4}\!n\,}\right)\,,\qquad\begin{array}[]{l}k=1,2,3,\ldots\\[2.84526pt] n\to\infty\,.\end{array}\qquad

In particular, for k=2k=2

1n!​∑l=1n|S1​(n,l)|l+2=1ln⁡n−1+γln2⁡n−π2−6​γ2−12​γ 6​ln3​n+O⁡(1ln4⁡n),n→∞\frac{1}{n!}\sum_{l=1}^{n}\frac{\big|S_{1}(n,l)\big|}{l+2}\,=\,\frac{1}{\,\ln n\,}-\frac{1+\gamma}{\,\ln^{2}\!n\,}-\frac{\,\pi^{2}-6\gamma^{2}-12\gamma\,}{\,6\ln^{3}\!n\,}+O\!\left(\frac{1}{\,\ln^{4}\!n\,}\right)\,,\qquad n\to\infty (135)

Similarly,

∑l=1nS1​(n,l)l+k=(−1)n​∫01xk−1​(−x)n​𝑑x∼(−1)n−1​(n−1)!n​∫01nz​(1−z)kΓ⁡(z)​𝑑z=(−1)n−1​(n−1)!n∑m=0k(km)(−1)m∫01zm​nzΓ⁡(z)dz,n→∞,\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\sum_{l=1}^{n}\frac{S_{1}(n,l)}{l+k}&\displaystyle=\,(-1)^{n}\!\int\limits_{0}^{1}\!x^{k-1}(-x)_{n}\,dx\,\sim\,\frac{\,(-1)^{n-1}(n-1)!\,}{n}\!\int\limits_{0}^{1}\!\frac{\,n^{z}(1-z)^{k}\,}{\Gamma(z)}\,dz\\[17.07164pt] &\displaystyle\quad=\,\frac{\,(-1)^{n-1}(n-1)!\,}{n}\sum_{m=0}^{k}\binom{k}{m}(-1)^{m}\!\int\limits_{0}^{1}\!\frac{\,z^{m}n^{z}\,}{\Gamma(z)}\,dz\,,\qquad n\to\infty\,,\end{array}

whence

1n!​∑l=1nS1​(n,l)l+k\displaystyle\displaystyle\frac{1}{n!}\sum_{l=1}^{n}\frac{S_{1}(n,l)}{l+k}\;\, ∼(−1)n−1n​∑m=0k(km)​(−1)m​{1ln⁡n+∑l=1∞(−1)llnl+1⁡n⋅[xmΓ⁡(x)]x=1(l)}\displaystyle\displaystyle\sim\,\frac{\,(-1)^{n-1}}{n}\sum_{m=0}^{k}\binom{k}{m}(-1)^{m}\left\{\frac{1}{\,\ln n\,}+\sum\limits_{l=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{l}}{\ln^{l+1}n}\cdot\left[\frac{x^{m}}{\Gamma(x)}\right]^{(l)}_{x=1}\right\}
=(−1)n−1n​{k!lnk+1⁡n−γ⁡(k+1)!lnk+2⁡n+O⁡(1lnk+3⁡n)},k=1,2,3,…n→∞,\displaystyle\displaystyle=\,\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n}\left\{\frac{k!}{\,\ln^{k+1}\!n\,}-\frac{\gamma\,(k+1)!}{\,\ln^{k+2}\!n\,}+O\!\left(\frac{1}{\,\ln^{k+3}\!n\,}\right)\!\right\}\,,\qquad\begin{array}[]{l}k=1,2,3,\ldots\\[2.84526pt] n\to\infty\,,\end{array}

In particular,

1n!​∑l=1nS1​(n,l)l+2=(−1)n−1n​{2ln3⁡n−6​γln4⁡n−2​(π2−6​γ2)ln5⁡n+O⁡(1ln6⁡n)},n→∞\frac{1}{n!}\sum_{l=1}^{n}\frac{S_{1}(n,l)}{l+2}\,=\,\frac{\,(-1)^{n-1}}{n}\left\{\frac{2}{\,\ln^{3}\!n\,}-\frac{6\gamma}{\,\ln^{4}\!n\,}-\frac{2(\pi^{2}-6\gamma^{2})}{\,\ln^{5}\!n\,}+O\!\left(\frac{1}{\,\ln^{6}\!n\,}\right)\!\right\}\,,\qquad n\to\infty (139)

Finally, we remark that different asymptotical aspects, in which are involved Stirling numbers, are also discussed, at different extents, in works of Jordan [75], [76, Chapt. IV], Moser & Wyman [103], Wilf [161], Temme [147], Hwang [72], Timashev [152], Grünberg [62] and Louchard [96]. Readers interested in a more deep study of general asymptotical methods might also wish to consult the following literature: [49, Chapt. I, § 4], [48], [115], [43].
